title.narrative: NDC Partnership's Center for Access to Climate Finance & FCDO

description.narrative: The Center will scale up and amplify the learning from the Pioneer Country pilots to enable systemic opportunities to improve climate finance. This will be done by disseminating evidence from Pioneer Countries, communicating, and amplifying best practices and lessons through the NDC Partnership and its broader network to shape improvements in policies and procedures of the international climate finance system. The Center will deliver global thought-leadership, policy analysis, evidence generation, lesson learning and knowledge sharing. Specifically, activities will be delivered across four main areas: Knowledge sharing and dissemination, System thinking and policy analysis, Governance and Outreach

The NDC Partnership is a global coalition, bringing together more than 200 members, including more than 120 countries, developed and developing, and nearly 100 institutions to deliver on ambitious climate action that helps achieve the Paris Agreement and drive sustainable development. Governments identify their NDC implementation priorities and the type of support that is needed to translate them into actionable policies and programs. Based on these requests, the membership offers a tailored package of expertise, technical assistance, and funding. This collaborative response provides developing countries with efficient access to a wide range of resources to adapt to and mitigate climate change and foster more equitable and sustainable development.

The primary test group of the Center activities are the Pioneer Countries (Rwanda, Uganda, Mauritius, Somalia, Bangladesh, Jamaica, Fiji), but leveraging the NDC Partnership's Work Program, the Center will deploy knowledge sharing activities hand in hand with the Partnership's country engagement strategy, and consider requests from non-Pioneer countries interested in replicating the Taskforce approach in the context of the Support Unit and Partnership's broader work. Climate Finance providers already engaged in the Taskforce, will also contribute to the Center's outputs through implementing the Taskforce Principles and Recommendation, including adopting harmonized processes to access, manage, and report on climate finance, aligning climate finance with national priorities and adopting innovative and agile approaches to deliver climate finance considering countries' contexts and capacities.

To improve the speed and scale at which climate vulnerable developing countries can access finance to deliver high-quality national climate and nature plans, the Taskforce on Access to Climate Finance (the Taskforce) was convened by the UK COP26 Presidency. The Center for Access to Climate Finance, which is an initiative of the Taskforce, funded by the UK Government, will collect and disseminate evidence from the Pioneer Country trials and gather and share lessons learned between climate vulnerable countries to help develop new solutions, scale-up successes, and advance global agenda on improved access to climate finance.

title.narrative: Indicator 2: Policy briefs and knowledge convenings respond to timely needs among the finance community reflect new knowledge generation or analysis.

comment.narrative: Activity 1: Develop policy briefs - Working through the expertise and skills within the NDC Partnership members and beyond, develop a series of policy briefs, with targeted actions, to help climate finance providers (and where appropriate, recipients) implement the Taskforce Principles and Recommendations. Policy briefs could focus on joint planning and financing frameworks, public expenditure, international aid architecture, blended finance instruments, global trends in climate finance, institutional strengthening, etc. The process for developing each policy brief will start with the mapping of a clear objective and audience. The NDC Partnership partners (including both members and non-members) tasked with the development of the brief will be chosen based on their understanding and engagement in the space, ensuring the brief is adding to the discourse and not repeating what has already been written. Where relevant, briefs will reference existing products, including NDC Partnership Plans and the World Bank's CCDRs, for example. Topics will be chosen based on progress made against the Principles and Recommendations as well needs identified across the Taskforce countries and more broadly, the Partnership.
Target achieved.

Activity 2: Virtual and in-person regional and global knowledge exchange among NDC Partnership members and beyond to discuss best practices. Virtual and in-person regional and global knowledge exchange among NDC Partnership members and beyond to discuss best practices, amplify learning and insights from the Taskforce's in-country work. This will include webinars as well as opportunities to engage with existing platforms like the Coalition of Finance Ministers for Climate Action (CFMCA) and to leverage existing forums like the COPs, Regional Climate Weeks, the SBs, the Global NDC Conference, the World Bank/IMF Annual and Spring Meetings, I4C, etc. Events will target key stakeholders, including private sector, MDBs, developed countries, as well as recipient countries.
Target exceeded.
